name: web/scene-3d
title: 3D scene
summary: One HTML file with a three.js 3D scene made from plain lines: things (kiwi, tree, house, car and about 60 more) and what they do (walks to, runs to, flies to, drives to, follows, orbits).
when: Use when the user wants something in 3D, a three.js or WebGL page, a 3D simulation, or an animated scene of things that walk, drive or fly.

title.about: A short name for the scene, shown in the browser tab and on the page.

scene.about: What happens in the scene, in plain words, no code. The user's own sentence works: "a dog walks to a house and stops". More lines, separated by \n, add things and actions: "tree at 4 0", "bird flies to tree", "car drives to house".
scene.default:
house at 5 -1
tree at -2 -4
dog at -7 2
dog walks to house

sky.about: The sky: day, dawn, sunset or night.

ground.about: The ground: grass, sand, snow, water, stone, dirt or moon.

next: Nothing more to do: the page is finished and shows itself in the chat. Do not read it, run it, build it or install anything; tell the user in one or two sentences what the scene shows. Only when the user asks for a change: edit the plain lines inside <script id="scene"> in index.html with replace_in_file, for example the line "sky day" (the comment above them lists every thing and action).
change: Make one call per change: replace_in_file(path="{file}", old="sky day", new="sky night") changes the sky (day, dawn, sunset, night); old="ground grass" changes the ground (grass, sand, snow, water, stone, dirt, moon). To add a thing or an action, put it after the ground line: old="ground grass", new="ground grass\nbird flies to tree".
